messages:
sasha: heads-up — since ~01:10 UTC pdx POP seeing p95+p99 RTT jitter and a small but consistent throughput drop. traces point at a mix of kernel-selector thrash + lots of tiny batches. anyone digging in?
infra-bot: alert: latency_spike detected on pdx-pop (route: public-eu-us-west). p95 increased 3x, p99 increased 4x. Incident ID: INC-2026-3457
marco: grabbing selector logs now. initial look: repeated kernel fallback cycles (latency-sensitive -> generic) every ~20-40s, coincides with the RTT spikes.
marco: snippet from selector logs:
```
[2026-06-12T01:11:22Z] selector: eval_latency=18ms eval_throughput=120qps chosen=latency_kernel
[2026-06-12T01:11:42Z] selector: eval_latency=45ms eval_throughput=60qps chosen=generic_kernel reason=kernel_mismatch
[2026-06-12T01:12:03Z] selector: eval_latency=16ms eval_throughput=140qps chosen=latency_kernel
```
marco: that oscillation lines up with the RTT jitter windows.
tien: ran a pprof flamegraph for the 01:10-01:20 window — inner-loop time is fine, but scheduling and small-batch overhead spikes. link: s3://redwood-perf/pdx/1789001234/flame.svg
olivia: quick note — we merged batching heuristic tweak earlier this week (PR #3421). changed max_batch_wait_ms from 10 -> 2 for default low-latency profile. that makes batches much smaller under jitter. could amplify kernel selector sensitivity.
olivia: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR-3421 (canary rolled 2026-06-11 22:00 UTC)
ryan: running traceroute from pdx-serv to model-host shows an intermittent route via SFO provider that adds ~12-18ms extra hop during spike windows. looks like an external routing flap / upstream path change.
ryan: traceroute snippet:
```
1  10.0.3.1 (10.0.3.1)  0.5 ms
2  198.51.100.1 (198.51.100.1)  1.2 ms
3  * * *
4  203.0.113.45 (203.0.113.45)  14.7 ms  <-- via SFO provider
5  203.0.113.78 (203.0.113.78)  15.2 ms
```
elena: if DNS is resolving to a peer that's routing via SFO, that explains jitter windows. any DNS TTL changes recently?
sasha: checked: edge DNS entries for pdx-pop had an older CNAME pointing at provider-b (ttl 300). provider-b had a change this morning. looks like some clients re-resolved and took the noisy path.
sasha: also, kvcache hit-rate dropped ~7% during spikes (eviction logs show short-lived TTL churn). small batches + more remote latency = shorter effective KV cache lifetime.
tien: agreed — smaller batches increase RPC frequency and reduce amortized KV hits. profiling shows KV lookup time contribution rose from 3% -> 12% of tail.
marco: kernel-selector uses recent latency samples to pick kernels. if network jitter creates transient high latencies, selector favors generic kernels which are slower on average for our common shapes, amplifying p99.
elena: mitigations: 1) pin kernel_policy=low_latency for pdx pop (force latency_kernel), 2) revert PR-3421 in canary (or increase max_batch_wait_ms to 8), 3) add DNS monitoring + reduce TTL fallback on edge records, 4) temporarily increase kvcache size to reduce evictions.
olivia: I can revert canary now. re-running the canary rollback patch.
olivia: rollback submitted and canary started (canary id: canary-842).
sasha: pinned kernel_policy -> low_latency on pdx-pop via runtime config (applied). watching.
infra-bot: action_log: kernel_policy pin applied to pdx-pop by sasha at 01:28 UTC. rollback of PR-3421 canary started by olivia at 01:29 UTC.
ryan: spoke to provider NOC — they confirm a partial route leak/peer misconfig around the SFO exchange between 01:05-01:20 UTC. they rolled an announcement and claim full convergence at ~01:25 UTC.
sasha: immediate effect — p95 back to baseline within ~120s of kernel pin + canary rollback. KV hit-rate recovering.
elena: follow-ups: 1) add a kernel-selector dampening parameter so single RTT blips don't force fallback, 2) add a batching heuristic that considers recent route stability / dns-change events, 3) tighter alerting for kvcache hit-rate regressions.
sasha: noted. created perf-ticket PERF-788 to track selector dampening + batching heuristics and DNS telemetry integration.
sasha: summary: root cause = external path change (provider route via SFO) + internal small-batch heuristic that made selector over-react -> fallback to suboptimal kernel -> amplified tail. mitigations applied (kernel pin + canary rollback + provider convergence). will monitor 24h. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: incident INC-2026-3457 status -> mitigated.
